title: I tried to build the Homeworld/Freelancer mashup of my dreams! A failed dark factory and 8 months in, it's finally done! These were the limits I found with the current tools.
author: MysteriousEar9986
selftext:
I just put out Eimyrja: The Last Fleet, an isometric space combat game for iPhone and iPad, and I didn’t write any of the code. I directed AI agents to do it, mostly Claude and then Codex for the last couple of weeks. It took about 12 weeks of real building, it’s been on the App Store since October 31, and it’s free. I wanted to share how it actually went, because it was pretty different from what I expected.

It started as a chat back in March. I pitched a space MMO for iPhone, got a normal production roadmap back, and told it I wanted this on an AI schedule instead. I spent the spring going back and forth on the design in chat and prototyping in Unity, and didn’t make my first commit until July.

The biggest thing I learned is that the agents are great at anything a test can check, and I was the only one who could check everything else. In August an agent told me a dialogue bug was fixed for the second time, and it still wasn’t. I got frustrated enough to threaten to move the whole project to OpenAI, and two months later I threatened Codex that I’d go back to Claude. Neither one was really the problem though. I was the only one who could actually see the game.

A few things made a big difference. Every time I made a decision, the agent wrote it into a short note that every other agent reads, and by the end there were around 120 of them. That’s the only reason agents that forget everything kept one game consistent for 12 weeks. I also had them build probes that take pictures from the game’s own camera and fly through every mission, and whenever a probe and my phone disagreed I went with the phone. And I got a lot more willing to delete things. If a player can’t reach it, it goes. Cutting the unused paint schemes alone halved the app size.

What didn’t work was anything about feel or look. That was round after round of me playing on my phone and reporting back. The worst was agents saying something was done when nobody had checked it, like a 60 fps claim on a phone that was running at 30, or frigates flying backwards because an agent overrode a check that was actually right. At one point I had to ask for a plain list of what was really on my phone and tell it not to lie. And honestly, installing my own game on my own phone ate more nights than any bug. One night I accused the agent of lying about Wi-Fi speeds, and almost an hour and a half later I figured out my phone was in low power mode.

The part I think this sub will care about most is the ships, because AI couldn’t make them. From April to October I tried 114 Meshy generations, a Blender cleanup workshop and a ship compiler with AI judges, and I didn’t approve a single one of the workshop’s 192 revisions. 78 of the 90 ships in the game come from bought Unity Asset Store packs. What AI did ship was the flat stuff - portraits, icons, ship paint, radio voices and most of the sound effects. It’s great at making a picture of a ship and bad at making a ship. I wrote up the whole ship saga here: [I tried to make AI build my spaceships](https://jamesktan.substack.com/p/i-tried-to-make-ai-build-my-spaceships)

My biggest fail was in October, when I tried to build a lights-out factory where agents build, test and submit the game with nobody watching. About 200 agents and 63M tokens later I had zero real store submissions, because every store test ran against a fake store. I killed it, and the small release kit that came out of it is what ships my builds now.

If I started over I’d get the game on a real phone on day one and never take an agent’s word that something’s fixed without a screenshot. I’d write every decision down where the agents will read it, have them build tools that can see the game, and keep one agent building and testing while the rest just edit. If an agent can’t see something it’ll guess, and it’ll tell you the guess is a fact.

As for the game itself, you wake up with a damaged ship and no memory and fight your way home through the space of five peoples who each remember the Collapse differently. There’s an 8-chapter campaign, a few single player modes including an experimental Hunted mode, and 2–4 player co-op. It’s free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad with no ads or in-app purchases, and Android is in progress: [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/eimyrja-the-last-fleet/id6816837471](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/eimyrja-the-last-fleet/id6816837471)

The trailer is on the game’s site: [https://www.eimyrja.gg](https://www.eimyrja.gg/)

I also wrote a much longer post-mortem with all the charts if you want the details: [2,573 prompts later: the Eimyrja post-mortem](https://jamesktan.substack.com/p/2573-prompts-later-the-eimyrja-post). Happy to go into any of it in the comments.

Question for the group: How is anyone making money on games these days? What's the end-game?
